title: [DETECTION] Libpairip and Google play integrity limitations
body:
**Provide the file**
Related example APKs
- https://apkcombo.com/chessbar/com.chessbar/download/apk
- https://apkcombo.com/burger-king/air.com.unit9.bkFrApp/download/apk

**Describe the detection issue**
I found a few things that seem wrong with the following rule:
https://github.com/dewee-dev/APKiD/commit/ecc9622da504292e5983c56851d11be32a1c0f48 related to issue https://github.com/rednaga/APKiD/issues/329

First, this protection mechanism does not seem to be directly related to Play Integrity API as much as to AIP (Automatic Integrity Protection), an option given to automatically check the APK's signature and other stuff (https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10183279?hl=en).
- My understanding is that the Play Integrity is a tool given to devs (com.google.android.play.core.integrity).
- Whereas AIP (com.pairip) is an automatic check added by Google as opt-in on the dev console.

Secondly, assuming the previous is true some apps avoid detection as they do not have libpairipcore.so (or libpairip.so) integrated but still have the licensing check automated on app launch. So there seems to be different levels of com.pairip, some with integrity verification mechanisms, obfuscation and licensing other with only licensing


**What I think should be done:**

1- Modify the entry for "play integrity" to "Pairip" or "Google AIP (Automatic Integrity Protection)".

2- Add a different entry for the limited "pairip" with only licensing

3- Add an entry for Google play integrity API which is also a protection tool for apps.
Some apps with it, my detection mecanism is simply looking for "com.google.android.play.core.integrity" after decompiling to java with **[[apklab](https://github.com/APKLab/APKLab)](https://github.com/APKLab/APKLab)**

## Examples

**Example 1: App without libpairipcore** https://apkcombo.com/chessbar/com.chessbar/download/apk
This app has a licensing check related to pairip, automatically tested on contentprovider.onCreate(). AndroidManifest.xml:
```xml
	<activity android:exported="false" android:name="com.pairip.licensecheck.LicenseActivity"/>
	<provider android:authorities="com.chessbar.com.pairip.licensecheck.LicenseContentProvider" android:exported="false" android:name="com.pairip.licensecheck.LicenseContentProvider"/>

```
But I could not find any other part like the VM or the libpairipcore.so, even libunity did not seem to include it. Although my research was limited.

This is not detected by APKiD although it is still pairip, even if only part of it. (Could be a library with the same name too technically, but I've found 40 something apps with the same situation)
